group: Valid input – satisfies schema

cases.expected: An empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no validation errors).
cases.description: The schema requires a string property "name". Supplying a JSON object that contains a valid "name" field should pass validation with no errors.

group: Missing required property – should produce a validation error

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing one message whose code is "required" and whose message mentions the missing property "name".
cases.description: The schema declares "name" as a required property. An empty object violates this rule, so the validator must return a validation message indicating the missing required field.

group: Type mismatch – root node is not an object

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing a message with code "type" indicating that the instance type (array) does not match the expected type (object).
cases.description: The schema expects the root node to be an object. Providing a JSON array should trigger a type‑validation error.

group: Null root node – defensive handling

cases.expected: Throws NullPointerException (or returns a Set containing a single message with code "null" depending on implementation).
cases.description: Calling validate(JsonNode) with a null argument tests the method’s null‑safety. The expected behavior is either an explicit NPE or a validation message indicating that the instance is null.

group: Schema with no validators – always succeeds

cases.expected: An empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no validation errors).
cases.description: When the JsonSchema instance is created from an empty schema (e.g., `{}`) it has no validators. Any JSON value, including a plain string, should validate successfully.

group: Enum validation – value not in enum

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing one message with code "enum" stating that the value "RED" is not one of the allowed values ["GREEN","BLUE"].
cases.description: The schema defines an enum of ["GREEN","BLUE"]. Supplying a string not present in the enum should trigger an enum validation error.

group: Multiple validation errors – missing required and type mismatch

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing two messages: one with code "type" because the instance is a number but an object is expected, and another with code "required" mentioning the missing property "name" (if the type validator runs before required).
cases.description: The schema expects an object with a required string property "name". Providing a plain number should cause both a type error and a required‑property error, testing that the validator aggregates multiple failures.

group: Boolean schema false – always fails

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing a single message with code "false" (or a generic error) indicating that the schema is boolean false and therefore any instance is invalid.
cases.description: When the JsonSchema is created from the literal boolean false, validation must always fail regardless of the instance.

group: Boolean schema true – always succeeds

cases.expected: An empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no validation errors).
cases.description: A schema that is the literal boolean true accepts any JSON value, including null, without producing validation messages.

group: Pattern validation – string does not match regex

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing one message with code "pattern" indicating that the value "abc123" does not match the required regular expression "^[A-Z]+$".
cases.description: The schema requires the string to consist only of uppercase letters. Supplying a mixed‑case alphanumeric string should trigger a pattern‑validation error.

group: Number range – value out of bounds

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing one message with code "maximum" stating that the value 150 exceeds the maximum allowed value 100.
cases.description: The schema defines a numeric maximum of 100. Providing a number larger than this limit should result in a maximum‑validation error.

group: Array length – too few items

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing one message with code "minItems" indicating that the array has 2 items but the minimum required is 3.
cases.description: The schema requires an array with at least 3 items. Supplying an array with only 2 items should raise a minItems validation error.

group: OneOf validation – none match

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing one message with code "oneOf" stating that the instance does not match any of the oneOf subschemas.
cases.description: The schema uses a oneOf with two alternatives (e.g., a string "yes" or a string "no"). Supplying a different string should cause a oneOf validation failure.

group: AnyOf validation – at least one matches (positive case)

cases.expected: An empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no validation errors).
cases.description: The schema defines anyOf with a numeric schema (minimum 0) and a string schema (pattern "^[a-z]+$"). Providing a valid number satisfies one of the alternatives, so validation succeeds.

group: Not validation – value matches prohibited schema

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing one message with code "not" indicating that the instance matches a schema that is explicitly prohibited.
cases.description: The schema contains a "not" clause that disallows the exact string "forbidden". Supplying that string should trigger a not‑validation error.

group: Conditional validation – if true then then clause enforced

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing one message with code "minimum" stating that the "discount" value -5 is less than the allowed minimum 0 (as required by the then‑schema).
cases.description: The schema uses an if/then construct: if "type" equals "premium" then "discount" must be >= 0. The instance satisfies the if condition but violates the then condition, leading to a minimum‑validation error.

group: AdditionalProperties false – extra property produces error

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing one message with code "additionalProperties" indicating that the property "age" is not allowed.
cases.description: The schema defines an object with a required property "name" and sets "additionalProperties": false. Supplying an extra property "age" should cause an additionalProperties validation error.

group: Format validation – invalid email address

cases.expected: A Set<ValidationMessage> containing one message with code "format" stating that the value does not match the email format.
cases.description: The schema specifies "format": "email" for a string property. Providing a string that is not a valid email address should trigger a format‑validation error.

group: Recursive anchor – self‑referential schema validates correctly

cases.expected: An empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no validation errors).
cases.description: The schema defines a recursive anchor "$recursiveAnchor": true and a property "node" that references the same schema. A nested structure respecting the schema should validate without stack overflow or errors.

group: Internal $ref – resolves to definition correctly

cases.expected: An empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no validation errors).
cases.description: The schema contains a $ref to an internal definition that enforces a pattern "^[a-z]{3}[0-9]{3}$". The provided string matches the pattern, testing correct resolution of internal $ref.

group: Relative $ref with $id – resolves base URI correctly

cases.expected: An empty Set<ValidationMessage> (no validation errors).
cases.description: The schema has an "$id": "http://example.com/schemas/main.json" and a property that $ref's "./sub.json". The referenced sub‑schema allows integers. Supplying an integer checks that relative $ref resolution using the base $id works.

group: Invalid $ref – unresolved reference

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException (or ValidationException) with a message indicating that the $ref "#/nonexistent" could not be resolved.
cases.description: The schema contains a $ref that points to a definition that does not exist. When validate(JsonNode) is invoked, the resolver should throw an exception rather than silently ignore the missing reference.

group: Unsupported keyword – unknown keyword in schema

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException with a message mentioning the unsupported keyword "unknownKeyword".
cases.description: A schema that includes a non‑standard keyword (e.g., "unknownKeyword": true) should cause the validator construction to fail, and validate(JsonNode) should propagate an IllegalArgumentException.

group: Invalid format value – unknown format specifier

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException with a message indicating that the format "unknown-format" is not supported.
cases.description: The schema declares a format that the library does not recognise. When validation runs, the library should raise an IllegalArgumentException rather than attempting to validate the value.

group: Circular $ref without recursive anchor – leads to StackOverflowError

cases.expected: StackOverflowError (or IllegalStateException if the implementation detects the cycle and aborts).
cases.description: Two schemas reference each other via $ref but neither declares "$recursiveAnchor": true. The validator will recurse indefinitely, eventually throwing a StackOverflowError (or a guarded IllegalStateException if cycle detection is implemented).

group: Schema with malformed $id – URL decoding error

cases.expected: UnsupportedEncodingException (wrapped in a RuntimeException) when the validator attempts to URL‑decode the malformed $id value.
cases.description: A schema that defines an "$id" containing characters that cannot be decoded with the default charset should cause URLDecoder.decode to throw UnsupportedEncodingException, which propagates during validation.
